product_context: Paraform (Agentic Hiring Platform) — not a Dune Security feature. Written for a design take-home exercise; source material is the exercise prompt, not an internal spec. Scoped entirely to the candidate page; broader recruiter dashboards are out of scope.
flows: Activity + context intake (log, filters, call lifecycle)
Call lifecycle: schedule (propose times / booking link) → review (per-call Para toggle + tags)
Ask Para assistant (cited Q&A + in-chat approval-gated actions)
Cross-opportunity hold (Para pauses its actions when an offer lands elsewhere)
Scored recommended opportunities (Proposed by Para AI)
key_fields: include-in-matching toggle (on / off, per context item)
context staleness flag (volatile items past threshold)
schedule-call mode (propose times / send booking link)
per-call 'use for Para AI' toggle + call tags
cross-opportunity hold state (Para-paused action, waiting on recruiter)
integrations: On-platform calls with automatic recording / transcription
Para AI matching layer (recommends scored matches; the recruiter's action and consent originates every submission)
open_questions_flagged: Should the Include-in-matching toggle default on or off for notes/calls? (proposed new control)
How does Para AI compute the match score shown on recommendations (e.g. 8/10), and how is it kept legible/trustworthy?
Which state changes trigger a cross-opportunity hold (offer confirmed vs. verbal vs. final round), and how long does Para hold before re-escalating?
Is a 60-90 day staleness threshold right for all volatile context, or should different fact types decay at different rates?
Is company-to-opportunity mapping reliable enough to hard-block same-company double submission, or should it be a soft warning?
Any candidate-facing view, or is the candidate strictly the subject? (assumed subject-only)
How should the candidate page hand off to Paraform's existing cross-candidate Para review/approve surface?
resolved_by_paraform: One shared candidate record per person (an earlier per-recruiter-silo assumption was wrong and was removed)
'Managing across multiple opportunities' = coordinating the roles the recruiter personally submitted the candidate to
Cross-recruiter duplicate submission to the same role is platform-prevented and out of scope for the take-home
Every submission originates from a recruiter's action and consent — Para AI never auto-submits
A consistent place to review/approve Para AI activity across candidates already exists; inline approvals roll up to it
Context today: structured insights from resume + LinkedIn, recruiter-added preferences, transcript-derived insights when calls are recorded
A private / exclude-from-Para control is a new distinction this design proposes, not existing behavior
confidence_notes: Single source (the take-home prompt itself) with no existing Figma or internal spec to cross-reference. Scope, actors, and edge cases were reasonably inferable from the prompt and the linked Passive Placements concept, but several judgment calls (default visibility rules, approval timeout window, conflict-detection mechanism) are design decisions made to produce a complete PRD rather than facts confirmed by the source. Updated 2026-07-11 with further product research indicating candidate profiles are owned per recruiter (not shared platform-wide) and that Para AI's matching reach can extend beyond opportunities the recruiter has directly pursued — this is a working hypothesis pending confirmation, not a PM-confirmed fact, and is tracked as open questions. Updated again 2026-07-11 with an IA refinement from design review: Opportunities as the default landing view, Profile split from Context, Action Queue merged inline, durable-vs-volatile context staleness — these are design decisions, not externally confirmed facts. Refocused 2026-07-14 onto the candidate page and expanded with the Activity tab, the on-platform call lifecycle (schedule → review with a per-call Para toggle and tags), scored recommended opportunities, the cross-opportunity hold, and the Ask Para assistant (cited Q&A plus in-chat approval-gated actions). Reconciled 2026-07-14 with Paraform's answers to clarifying questions (see resolved_by_paraform): there is one shared candidate record (an earlier per-recruiter-silo assumption was removed); coordination is scoped to the recruiter's own submissions; every submission originates from recruiter action/consent (Para never auto-submits); cross-recruiter dedup is platform-handled; a consistent Para review/approve surface already exists; and the private/include-in-matching control is a new distinction this design proposes. Remaining open items are design-detail on those proposed distinctions, not scope/architecture.
